newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate remains at 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate remains at 10 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate remained at around 10 percent at the close on Tuesday, with no fresh lending by Bank Negara seen, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 9.5 and 13 percent.
Agent banks of Bank Negara were lending one-month and overnight funds on Monday. Dealers believed the funds were Bank Negara's.
"There's no sign of them today," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "We are still confused over where rates are heading."
Earlier, interbank rates fell on perception that the central bank wants to see lower rates.
One-week money was at 13/15 percent, against 25 percent on Monday.
One-month rate was at 9/10 percent against 15/17 percent.
Rates also came off ahead of maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Wednesday.
Malaysia's Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday the country did not favour a high interest rate regime in the long term.

"I don't think we are for (a) continued rise in interest rates, or a strong interest rate regime," he said, adding that the recent rise in interest rates was prompted by the recent speculative selling of the ringgit.

Dealers said lending by Bank Negara was needed to ease the shortage of ringgit funds following the central bank's heavy buying of the currency last week to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers were estimating between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit was drained from the system.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rose across the board to reflect falling interbank rates.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up six points to 92.38, or an implied yield of 7.62 percent.
The December contract also rose six to 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
